contenido: 1. The Gospel of life is at the center of Jesus' message. Welcomed with love every day by the Church, it is announced with fearless fidelity as good news to men of all times and cultures.

2. Man is called to a fullness of life that goes beyond the dimensions of his earthly existence, since it consists of participating in the very life of God. The sublime of this supernatural vocation manifests the greatness and value of human life even in its temporal phase. In effect, life in time is a basic condition, initial moment and integral part of the entire unitary process of human life. A process that, unexpectedly and undeservedly, is illuminated by the promise and renewed by the gift of divine life, which will reach its full realization in eternity ( [+[0]+] ). At the same time, this supernatural call precisely underlines the relative character of the earthly life of man and woman. In truth, this is not "ultimate" reality, but rather "penultimate"; It is a sacred reality, which is entrusted to us so that we can guard it with a sense of responsibility and bring it to perfection in love and in the gift of ourselves to God and our brothers.

3. Each person, precisely by virtue of the mystery of the Word of God made flesh ([+[0]+]), is entrusted to the maternal care of the Church. Therefore, every threat to the dignity and life of man reverberates at the very heart of the Church, affects the core of its faith in the redeeming incarnation of the Son of God, and compromises it in its mission of announcing the Gospel of life throughout the world and to every creature ([+[1]+]).

4. Unfortunately, this alarming panorama, instead of decreasing, is rather increasing. With the new perspectives opened by scientific and technological progress, new forms of aggression against the dignity of the human being emerge, at the same time that a new cultural situation is being outlined and consolidated, which gives attacks on life an unprecedented and "one might say" even more iniquitous aspect, causing further and serious concerns: broad sectors of public opinion justify some attacks on life in the name of the rights of individual freedom, and on this assumption They seek not only impunity, but even authorization from the State, in order to practice them with absolute freedom and also with the free intervention of health structures.

5. The Extraordinary Consistory of Cardinals, held in Rome from April 4 to 7, 1991, was dedicated to the problem of threats to human life in our time. After a broad and profound debate on the topic and on the challenges presented to the entire human family and, in particular, to the Christian community, the Cardinals, with a unanimous vote, asked me to ratify, with the authority of the Successor of Peter, the value of human life and its inviolable character, in relation to the current circumstances and the attacks that threaten it today.

6. In deep communion with each of my brothers and sisters in the faith, and encouraged by a sincere friendship towards all, I want to meditate again and announce the Gospel of life, splendor of truth that illuminates consciences, clear light that heals the darkened gaze, inexhaustible source of perseverance and courage to face the ever new challenges that we find on our path.

7. « It was not God who caused death nor does he delight in the destruction of the living; He created everything so that it could subsist... Because God created man for incorruptibility, he made him the image of his own nature; but through envy of the devil death entered the world, and those who belong to him experience it » ( [+[0]+] ).

8. Cain was “very angry” and his face was “cast down” because the Lord “looked favorably upon Abel and his oblation” ([+[0]+]). The biblical text does not say the reason why God preferred Abel's sacrifice to Cain's; However, he clearly indicates that, even though he preferred Abel's oblation, he did not interrupt his dialogue with Cain. He rebukes him, reminding him of his freedom from evil: man is not predestined to evil. Certainly, like Adam, he is tempted by the evil power of sin that, like a ferocious beast, is lurking at the door of his heart, waiting to pounce on its prey. But Cain is free from sin. You can and must dominate it: "Like a beast that covets you, and whom you must dominate" ([+[1]+]).

9. God cannot leave the crime unpunished: from the ground on which it was spilled, the blood of the murdered cries out for justice to God ( [+[0]+] ). From this text the Church has derived the name "sins that cry out for revenge in the presence of God" and among them has included, first of all, voluntary homicide. 12 For the Hebrews, as for many other peoples of antiquity, life is found in the blood, better yet, "the blood is the life" ([+[1]+]) and life, especially human life, belongs only to God: therefore whoever attacks the life of man, in some way attacks God himself.

10. The Lord says to Cain: «What have you done? You hear your brother's blood crying out to me from the ground » ( [+[0]+] ). The voice of the blood shed by men does not cease to cry, from generation to generation, acquiring diverse and always new tones and accents.

11. But our attention wants to concentrate, in particular, on another type of attacks, related to nascent and terminal life, which present new characteristics compared to the past and raise problems of singular gravity, due to the fact that they tend to lose, in the collective conscience, the character of "crime" and to paradoxically assume that of "right", to the point of seeking true legal recognition by the State and subsequent execution through the free intervention of the same health agents. These attacks hit human life in situations of maximum precariousness, when it is deprived of any capacity for defense. Even more serious is the fact that, to a large extent, they occur precisely within and through the work of the family, which is constitutively called to be, however, a "sanctuary of life."

12. In fact, if many serious aspects of the current social problems can explain in a certain way the climate of widespread moral uncertainty and sometimes mitigate objective responsibility in people, it is no less true that we are facing a broader reality, which can be considered as a true and authentic structure of sin, characterized by the spread of a culture contrary to solidarity, which in many cases is configured as a true "culture of death." This structure is actively promoted by strong cultural, economic and political currents, carriers of a conception of society based on efficiency. Looking at things from this point of view, one can speak, in a certain sense, of a war of the powerful against the weak. The life that would require more welcome, love and care is considered useless, or considered an unbearable burden and, therefore, despised in many ways. Whoever, with his illness, his disability or, more simply, with his very presence, calls into question the well-being and lifestyle of the most advantaged, tends to be seen as an enemy who must be defended or eliminated. Thus a kind of "conspiracy against life" is unleashed, which affects not only specific people in their individual, family or group relationships, but goes further, harming and altering, at a global level, the relations between peoples and States.

13. To facilitate the spread of abortion, huge sums have been and continue to be invested to obtain pharmaceutical products, which make the death of the fetus possible in the womb, without the need to resort to the help of a doctor. The same scientific research on this point seems almost exclusively concerned with obtaining products that are increasingly simpler and more effective against life and, at the same time, capable of removing abortion from all forms of control and social responsibility.

14. Also the different techniques of artificial reproduction, which would seem to be put at the service of life and which are often practiced with this intention, in reality give rise to new attacks on life. Beyond the fact that they are morally unacceptable since they separate procreation from the integrally human context of the marital act, 14 these techniques register high percentages of failure. This affects not so much fertilization as the subsequent development of the embryo, exposed to the risk of death generally in a very short time. Furthermore, embryos are frequently produced in numbers greater than those necessary for implantation in the woman's womb, and these so-called "supernumerary embryos" are subsequently suppressed or used for research that, under the pretext of scientific or medical progress, actually reduces human life to simple "biological material" that can be freely disposed of.

15. No less serious threats also affect the incurably ill and the terminally ill, in a social and cultural context that, making it more difficult to face and endure suffering, exacerbates the temptation to solve the problem of suffering by eliminating it at its roots, anticipating death to the moment considered most opportune.

16. Another current phenomenon, in which threats and attacks on life frequently come together, is demographics. This presents different modalities in different parts of the world: in rich and developed countries there is a worrying reduction or fall in births; Poor countries, on the other hand, generally present a high rate of population increase, which is difficult to bear in a context of less economic and social development, or even serious underdevelopment. Given the overpopulation of poor countries, there is a lack, at the international level, of global measures - serious family and social policies, cultural development programs and fair production and distribution of resources - while anti-natalist policies continue to be carried out.

17. Today's humanity offers us a truly alarming spectacle, if we consider not only the various areas in which attacks on life occur, but also their singular numerical proportion, together with the multiple and powerful support they receive from a vast public opinion, frequent legal recognition and the involvement of a part of health personnel.

18. The panorama described must be considered taking into account not only the death phenomena that characterize it, but also the multiple causes that determine it. The Lord's question: «What have you done? » ( [+[0]+] ) seems like an invitation to Cain to go beyond the materiality of his homicidal gesture, and understand its full gravity in the motivations that were at its origin and in the consequences that follow.
19. Where are the roots of such a surprising contradiction?

20. With this conception of freedom, social coexistence deteriorates profoundly. If the promotion of one's own self is understood in terms of absolute autonomy, one inevitably arrives at the denial of the other, considered an enemy against whom to defend oneself. In this way, society becomes a set of individuals placed next to each other, but without reciprocal ties: each wants to assert itself independently of the others, even making its interests prevail. However, faced with the analogous interests of others, one is forced to seek any form of compromise if the maximum possible freedom in society is to be guaranteed to each person. Thus, all reference to common values ​​and an absolute truth for everyone disappears; Social life enters the quicksand of absolute relativism. So everything is agreeable, everything is negotiable: even the first of the fundamental rights, that of life.

21. In the search for the deepest roots of the struggle between the "culture of life" and the "culture of death", it is not enough to stop at the perverse idea of ​​freedom mentioned above. It is necessary to get to the center of the drama experienced by contemporary man: the eclipse of the sense of God and man, characteristic of the social and cultural context dominated by secularism, which with its penetrating tentacles never ceases to test, at times, the Christian communities themselves. Whoever allows himself to be infected by this atmosphere easily enters the whirlwind of a terrible vicious circle: losing the sense of God, we also tend to lose the sense of man, his dignity and his life. In turn, the systematic violation of the moral law, especially in the serious field of respect for human life and its dignity, produces a kind of progressive obfuscation of the ability to perceive the life-giving and saving presence of God.

22. For this reason, when the sense of God is lost, the sense of man is also threatened and contaminated, as the Second Vatican Council clearly states: "The creature without the Creator disappears... Furthermore, by forgetting God the creature itself is obscured."17 Man can no longer be understood as "mysteriously other" with respect to other earthly creatures; It is considered as one of many living beings, as an organism that, at most, has reached a very high stage of perfection. Enclosed in the restricted horizon of his materiality, he is thus reduced to "a thing", and no longer perceives the transcendent character of his "existence as a man." He no longer considers life as a splendid gift from God, a "sacred" reality entrusted to his responsibility and, therefore, to his loving custody, to his "veneration." Life becomes simply "a thing", which man claims as his exclusive property, totally dominable and manipulable.

23. The eclipse of the sense of God and man inevitably leads to practical materialism, in which individualism, utilitarianism and hedonism proliferate. The perennial validity of what the Apostle wrote is also manifested here: "Since they did not see fit to keep the true knowledge of God, God gave them over to their foolish minds, to do what is not appropriate" ([+[0]+]). Thus, the values ​​of being are replaced by those of having. The only goal that counts is the achievement of one's own material well-being. The so-called "quality of life" is interpreted mainly or exclusively as economic efficiency, disordered consumerism, beauty and enjoyment of physical life, forgetting the deeper "relational, spiritual and religious" dimensions of existence.

24. In the depths of the moral conscience, the eclipse of the meaning of God and man occurs, with all its multiple and disastrous consequences for life. Above all, the conscience of each person is questioned, who in their uniqueness and unrepeatability stands alone before God. 18 But, in a certain sense, the "moral conscience" of society is also questioned. This is in some way responsible, not only because it tolerates or favors behaviors contrary to life, but also because it feeds the "culture of death", creating and consolidating true and authentic "structures of sin" against life. Moral conscience, both individual and social, is today subject, also due to the strong influence of many media of social communication, to a very serious and mortal danger, that of confusion between good and evil in relation to the same fundamental right to life. Unfortunately, much of today's society resembles the one Paul describes in the Letter to the Romans. It is made up "of men who imprison the truth in injustice" ([+[0]+]): having renounced God and believing they could build the earthly city without needing Him, they "became confused in their reasoning" so that "their foolish heart was darkened" ([+[1]+]); «Boasting themselves as wise they became stupid» ([+[2]+]), they became authors of works worthy of death and «not only do they practice them, but they approve of those who commit them» ([+[3]+]). When conscience, this luminous eye of the soul ([+[4]+]), calls "evil good and good evil" ([+[5]+]), it is already moving towards its most disturbing degradation and towards the darkest moral blindness.

25. «You hear your brother's blood crying out to me from the ground» ([+[0]+]). It is not only the blood of Abel, the first innocent murdered, that cries out to God, source and defender of life. Also the blood of every man killed after Abel is a cry that rises to the Lord. In an absolutely unique way, the blood of Christ cries out to God, of whom Abel in his innocence is a prophetic figure, as the author of the Letter to the Hebrews reminds us: "You, however, have drawn near to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God... to the mediator of a New Covenant, and to the purifying sprinkling of a blood that speaks better than that of Abel" ([+[1]+]).

26. In reality, there is no shortage of signs that anticipate this victory in our societies and cultures, despite being strongly marked by the "culture of death." Therefore, a unilateral image would be given, which could lead to sterile discouragement, if, along with the denunciation of threats to life, the positive signs that exist in the current situation of humanity are not presented.

27. In the face of legislation that has allowed abortion and attempts, emerging here and there, to legalize euthanasia, movements and initiatives to raise social awareness in favor of life have appeared throughout the world. When, in accordance with their authentic inspiration, they act with certain firmness but without resorting to violence, these movements favor a more widespread and profound awareness of the value of life, requesting and making a more decisive commitment to its defense.

28. This horizon of lights and shadows must make us all fully aware that we are facing an enormous and dramatic clash between good and evil, death and life, the "culture of death" and the "culture of life." We are not only "before", but necessarily "in the middle" of this conflict: we are all involved and forced to participate, with the unavoidable responsibility to unconditionally choose in favor of life.

29. Faced with the innumerable and serious threats to life in the contemporary world, we could feel overwhelmed by a sense of insurmountable helplessness: good can never be strong enough to overcome evil!

30. Therefore, with our gaze fixed on the Lord Jesus we want to hear from Him again "the words of God" ([+[0]+]) and meditate again on the Gospel of life. The deepest and most original meaning of this meditation on the revealed message about human life has been expounded by the apostle John, at the beginning of his First Letter: "What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we contemplated and our hands touched concerning the Word of life - for the Life was manifested, and we have seen it and bear witness and proclaim to you eternal Life, which was turned towards the Father and was manifested to us - what We have seen and heard, we announce it to you, so that you also may be in communion with us » ( [+[1]+] ).

31. In reality, the evangelical fullness of the message about life was already prepared in the Old Testament. It is above all in the vicissitudes of the Exodus, the foundation of the Old Testament experience of faith, where Israel discovers the value of life in the eyes of God. When he seems already doomed to extermination, because the threat of death extends to all his newborn males ( [+[0]+] ), the Lord reveals himself to him as a savior, capable of ensuring a future for those who are without hope. Thus a clear conscience is born in Israel: its life is not at the mercy of a pharaoh who can use it with despotic discretion; On the contrary, it is the object of a tender and strong love on the part of God.

32. The experience of the people of the Alliance is repeated in that of all the "poor" who encounter Jesus of Nazareth. Just as the "life-loving" God ( [+[0]+] ) had comforted Israel in the midst of dangers, so now the Son of God announces, to all who feel threatened and impeded in their existence, that their lives are also a good to which the love of the Father gives meaning and value.

33. In the life of Jesus itself, from beginning to end, there is this unique "dialectic" between the experience of the precariousness of human life and the affirmation of its value. In fact, precariousness marks the life of Jesus from his birth. It certainly finds acceptance among the righteous, who joined Mary's determined and joyful "yes" ([+[0]+]). But he also immediately feels the rejection of a world that becomes hostile and looks for the child "to kill him" ([+[1]+]), or that remains indifferent and distracted by the fulfillment of the mystery of this life that enters the world: "they had no room in the lodging" ([+[2]+]). From the contrast between threats and insecurities, on the one hand, and the strength of God's gift, on the other, the glory that radiates from the house of Nazareth and the manger of Bethlehem shines with greater intensity: this life that is born is salvation for all humanity ( [+[3]+] ).
34. Life is always good. This is an intuition or, rather, a fact of experience, whose deep reason man is called to understand.

35. The Yahwist account of creation also expresses the same conviction. Indeed, this ancient narrative speaks of a divine breath that is infused into man so that he may have life: "The Lord God formed man with dust from the ground, breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living being" ([+[0]+]).

36. Unfortunately, God's magnificent project is obscured by the emergence of sin in history. With sin, man rebels against the Creator, ending up idolizing creatures: "They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and they worshiped and served the creature instead of the Creator" ([+[0]+]). In this way, the human being not only disfigures the image of God in himself, but is also tempted to offend it in others, replacing relationships of communion with attitudes of distrust, indifference, enmity, reaching homicidal hatred. When God is not recognized as God, the deep meaning of man is betrayed and the communion between men is harmed.

37. The life that the Son of God has come to give to men is not reduced to mere existence in time. Life, which has always been "in him" and is "the light of men" ([+[0]+]), consists in being begotten by God and participating in the fullness of his love: "To all who received him he gave power to become children of God, to those who believe in his name; who was not born of blood, nor of the desire of the flesh, nor of the desire of man, but was born of God » ( [+[1]+] ).

38. Therefore, eternal life is the very life of God and at the same time the life of the children of God. A new amazement and boundless gratitude necessarily take hold of the believer in the face of this unexpected and ineffable truth that comes to us from God in Christ. The believer makes his own the words of the apostle John: "See what love the Father has had for us to call us children of God, for we are!... Dear ones, now we are children of God and it has not yet been revealed what we will be. We know that when he appears, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is » ( [+[0]+] ).

39. Man's life comes from God, it is his gift, his image and imprint, participation in his vital breath. Therefore, God is the only lord of this life: man cannot dispose of it. God himself affirms this to Noah after the flood: "I promise you to claim your own blood: I will claim it from every animal and from man: from each and every one I will claim the human soul" ([+[0]+]). The biblical text is concerned with highlighting how the sacredness of life has its foundation in God and in his creative action: "For in the image of God He made man" ([+[1]+]).

40. From the sacredness of life its inviolable character derives, inscribed from the beginning in the heart of man, in his conscience. The question "What have you done?" » ([+[0]+]), with which God addresses Cain after he had killed his brother Abel, presents the experience of each man: deep in his conscience he is always called to respect the inviolable character of life – his own and that of others – as a reality that does not belong to him, because it is the property and gift of God the Creator and Father.

41. The commandment "thou shalt not kill," included and deepened in the positive precept of love for one's neighbor, is confirmed by the Lord Jesus in all its validity. To the rich young man who asks: «Master, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life? », he answers: «If you want to enter life, keep the commandments» ([+[0]+]). And he cites, as first, the "thou shalt not kill" ([+[1]+]). In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus demands from the disciples a justice superior to that of the scribes and Pharisees also in the field of respect for life: «You have heard that it was said to the ancestors: You shall not kill; and whoever kills will be convicted before the court. For I tell you: Anyone who is angry with his brother will be brought to justice before the court" ([+[2]+]).

42. Defending and promoting, respecting and loving life is a task that God entrusts to each man, calling him, as his palpitating image, to participate in the sovereignty that He has over the world: « And God blessed them, and God said to them: "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and over every animal that creeps on the earth" » ([+[0]+] ).

43. A certain participation of man in the sovereignty of God is also manifested in the specific responsibility that is entrusted to him in relation to properly human life. It is a responsibility that reaches its apex in the gift of life through procreation by man and woman in marriage, as the Second Vatican Council reminds us: "The same God, who said "it is not good for man to be alone" ([+[0]+]) and who "made man from the beginning, male and female" ([+[1]+]), wanting to communicate to him a certain special participation in his own creative work, blessed the man and the woman saying: "Be fruitful and multiply" ([+[2]+]).30

44. Human life is in a very precarious situation when it comes into the world and when it leaves time to reach eternity. Exhortations to care and respect are very present in the Word of God – especially in relation to existence marked by illness and old age. If there is a lack of direct and explicit calls to safeguard human life in its origins, especially life not yet born, as well as that which is close to its end, this is easily explained by the fact that the mere possibility of offending, attacking or even denying life under these conditions falls outside the religious and cultural horizon of the people of God.

45. The revelation of the New Testament confirms the indisputable recognition of the value of life from its beginnings. The exaltation of fertility and the diligent expectation of life resonate in the words with which Elizabeth rejoices at her pregnancy: "The Lord... deigned to take away my reproach among men" ([+[0]+]). The value of the person from his conception is celebrated even more vividly in the encounter between the Virgin Mary and Elizabeth, and between the two children they carry in their womb. It is precisely them, the children, who reveal the arrival of the messianic era: in their encounter the redeeming force of the presence of the Son of God among men begins to act. « Very soon – writes Saint Ambrose – the benefits of Mary's arrival and the presence of the Lord are manifested... Elizabeth was the first to hear the voice, but John was the first to experience the grace, because Elizabeth listened according to the faculties of nature, but John, on the other hand, rejoiced because of the mystery. Isabel felt the proximity of Mary, Juan that of the Lord; The woman heard the woman's greeting, the son felt the presence of the Son; They proclaim grace, they, living it internally, ensure that their mothers take advantage of this gift to such an extent that, with a double miracle, both begin to prophesy under the inspiration of their own children. The child leaped for joy and the mother was filled with the Holy Spirit, but the mother was not enriched before the son, but after the son was filled, the mother was also filled. "36

46. Also with regard to the last moments of existence, it would be anachronistic to expect from biblical revelation an express reference to the current problem of respect for the elderly and sick, and an explicit condemnation of attempts to violently anticipate their end. Indeed, we are in a cultural and religious context that is not affected by these temptations, but rather, with regard to the elderly, recognizes in their wisdom and experience an irreplaceable wealth for the family and society.

47. The mission of Jesus, with the numerous healings carried out, shows how God also cares about the bodily life of man. «Physician of the flesh and of the spirit»,37 Jesus was sent by the Father to announce the good news to the poor and to heal broken hearts ([+[0]+]). By later sending his disciples into the world, he entrusts them with a mission in which the healing of the sick accompanies the announcement of the Gospel: "Go proclaiming that the Kingdom of Heaven is near." Heal the sick, raise the dead, purify lepers, cast out demons » ( [+[1]+] ).

48. Life has its truth written indelibly in itself. Man, accepting the gift of God, must commit to maintaining life in this truth, which is essential to him. Distancing yourself from it is equivalent to condemning yourself to a lack of meaning and unhappiness, with the consequence of also being able to be a threat to the existence of others, once the barriers that guarantee respect and defense of life in each situation are broken.

49. The history of Israel shows how difficult it is to maintain fidelity to the law of life, which God has inscribed in the hearts of men and delivered on Sinai to the people of the Covenant. In the search for alternative life projects to God's plan, the Prophets strongly claim that only the Lord is the authentic source of life. Thus Jeremiah writes: "My people have done double evil: they have left me, the Spring of living waters, to make cisterns for themselves, cracked cisterns, which cannot hold water" ([+[0]+]). The Prophets point the accusing finger at those who despise life and violate people's rights: "They trample the heads of the weak in the dust of the earth" ([+[1]+]); «They have filled this place with the blood of innocents» ([+[2]+]). Among them, the prophet Ezekiel censures the city of Jerusalem several times, calling it "the bloody city" ([+[3]+]), "a city that sheds blood in your midst" ([+[4]+]).

50. At the end of this chapter, in which we have meditated on the Christian message about life, I would like to stop with each of you to contemplate the One whom you passed through and who draws everyone to Himself ( [+[0]+] ). Looking at "the spectacle" of the cross ([+[1]+]) we can discover in this glorious tree the fulfillment and full revelation of the entire Gospel of life.

51. There is still another concrete fact that catches my attention and makes me meditate with emotion: « When Jesus took the vinegar, he said: "It is finished." And bowing his head he gave up the spirit. ( [+[0]+] ). And the Roman soldier "pierced his side with a spear and immediately blood and water came out" ([+[1]+]).

52. « At this one came to him and said, "Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?" » ( [+[0]+] ). Jesus responds: "If you want to enter life, keep the commandments" ([+[1]+]). The Master speaks of eternal life, that is, of participation in the very life of God. This life is reached by observing the commandments of the Lord, including also the commandment "thou shalt not kill." Precisely this is the first precept of the Decalogue that Jesus reminds the young man who asks what commandments he should observe: « Jesus said: "You shall not kill, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal..." » ([+[2]+] ).

53. « Human life is sacred because from its beginning it involves "the creative action of God" and always remains in a special relationship with the Creator, its only end. Only God is Lord of life from its beginning to its end: no one, under any circumstances, can claim the right to directly kill an innocent human being. "41 With these words the Instruction Donum Vitae exposes the central content of God's revelation on the sacred and inviolable character of human life.

54. Explicitly, the precept "thou shalt not kill" has a strong negative content: it indicates the limit that can never be transgressed. Implicitly, however, it leads to a positive attitude of absolute respect for life, helping to promote it and progress along the path of love that gives, welcomes and serves. The people of the Alliance, even with slowness and contradictions, were progressively maturing in this direction, thus preparing themselves for the great announcement of Jesus: love for one's neighbor is a commandment similar to that of love for God; «On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets» ([+[0]+]). «The... you shall not kill... and all the other precepts - Saint Paul points out - are summarized in this formula: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself" ([+[1]+]). The precept "thou shalt not kill", assumed and carried to its fullness in the New Law, is an inalienable condition to be able to "enter into life" ([+[2]+]). In this same perspective, the words of the apostle John are also compelling: “Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer; and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him » ( [+[3]+] ).

55. It should not surprise us: killing a human being, in whom the image of God is present, is a particularly serious sin. Only God is the owner of life! Always, however, in the face of the multiple and often dramatic situations that individual and social life presents, the reflection of believers has tried to know in a more complete and profound way what the commandment of God prohibits and prescribes. 43 In fact, there are situations in which the values ​​proposed by the Law of God appear as a true paradox. This is the case, for example, of self-defense, in which the right to protect one's own life and the duty not to harm that of another are, specifically, difficult to reconcile. Without a doubt, the intrinsic value of life and the duty to love oneself no less than others are the basis of a true right to self-defense. The same demanding precept of love for one's neighbor, formulated in the Old Testament and confirmed by Jesus, assumes love for oneself as one of the terms of comparison: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself" ([+[0]+]). Therefore, no one could renounce the right to defend oneself because of little love for life or oneself, but only moved by a heroic love, which deepens and transforms love for oneself, according to the spirit of the evangelical beatitudes ( [+[1]+] ) in the oblative radicality whose sublime example is the Lord Jesus himself.

56. Within this horizon is also the problem of the death penalty, with respect to which there is, both in the Church and in civil society, a progressive tendency to request a very limited application and even its total abolition. The problem is framed in the perspective of a criminal justice that is increasingly in accordance with the dignity of man and therefore, ultimately, with God's plan for man and society. In effect, the penalty that society imposes "has as its first effect that of compensating for the disorder introduced by the offense."46 The public authority must repair the violation of personal and social rights by imposing on the offender an adequate atonement for the crime, as a condition for being readmitted to the exercise of one's freedom. In this way, the authority also achieves the objective of preserving public order and the safety of people, but not without offering the prisoner himself encouragement and help to correct himself and make amends. 47

57. If such great attention is paid to respect for all life, including that of the prisoner and that of the unjust aggressor, the commandment "thou shalt not kill" has absolute value when it refers to the innocent person. All the more so if it is a weak and defenseless human being, who only finds his radical defense against the arbitrariness and arrogance of others in the absolute force of God's commandment.

58. Among all the crimes that man can commit against life, procured abortion has characteristics that make it particularly serious and ignominious. The Second Vatican Council defines it, along with infanticide, as "heinous crimes."54

59. In addition to the mother, other persons are frequently involved in the decision on the death of an unborn child. First of all, the father of the child may be guilty, not only when he expressly induces the woman to have an abortion, but also when he indirectly favors this decision of hers by leaving her alone to face the problems of pregnancy: 55 in this way the family is mortally wounded and its nature as a community of love and its vocation to be a "sanctuary of life" is profaned. We cannot forget the pressures that sometimes come from a broader context of family and friends. Not infrequently, the woman is subjected to such strong pressures that she feels psychologically forced to give in to abortion: there is no doubt that in this case moral responsibility particularly affects those who have directly or indirectly forced her to have an abortion. Doctors and health personnel are also responsible when they put the competence acquired to promote life at the service of death.

60. Some try to justify abortion by arguing that the fruit of conception, at least up to a certain number of days, cannot yet be considered a personal human life. In reality, "from the moment the egg is fertilized, a new life is inaugurated that is not that of the father or the mother, but that of a new human being that develops on its own." He will never become human if he has not been since then. To this age-old evidence... modern genetics provides precious confirmation. It shows that from the first moment the program of what that living being will be is set: a person, an individual with its characteristics already well determined. With fertilization begins the adventure of a human life, whose main capacities require time to develop and be able to act. "57 Although the presence of a spiritual soul cannot be deduced from the observation of any experimental data, the same conclusions of science on the human embryo offer "a precious indication to rationally discern a personal presence from this first emergence of human life: how could a human individual not be a human person? »58

61. The texts of Sacred Scripture, which never speak of voluntary abortion and, therefore, do not contain direct and specific condemnations in this regard, present the human being in the womb in such a way that they logically demand that the divine commandment "thou shalt not kill" be extended to this case as well.

62. The most recent pontifical Magisterium has reaffirmed this common doctrine with great vigor. In particular, Pius XI in the Encyclical Casti connubii rejected the alleged justifications for abortion; 65 Pius 66 John XXIII reaffirmed that human life is sacred, because "from the moment it emerges, it directly implies the creative action of God."67 The Second Vatican Council, as I have already recalled, condemned abortion with great severity: "life must be protected with the utmost care from conception; “Both abortion and infanticide are heinous crimes.”68

63. The moral assessment of abortion must also be applied to recent forms of intervention on human embryos that, while seeking legitimate ends in themselves, inevitably entail their destruction. This is the case of experiments with embryos, which are increasingly expanding in the field of biomedical research and are legally admitted by some States. If "interventions on the human embryo are lawful as long as they respect the life and integrity of the embryo, do not expose it to disproportionate risks, and have as their purpose its cure, the improvement of its health conditions or its individual survival",74 it must be stated, however, that the use of human embryos or fetuses as objects of experimentation constitutes a crime in consideration of their dignity as human beings, who have the right to the same respect due to the already born child and to all person. 75

64. At the other end of existence, man finds himself faced with the mystery of death. Today, due to progress in medicine and in a cultural context often closed to transcendence, the experience of death presents itself with some new characteristics. In fact, when the tendency prevails to appreciate life only to the extent that it gives pleasure and well-being, suffering appears as an unbearable threat, from which it is necessary to get rid of at all costs. Death, considered "absurd" when it unexpectedly interrupts a life still open to a future rich in possible interesting experiences, becomes, on the contrary, a "claimed liberation" when it is considered that existence is no longer meaningless because it is immersed in pain and inexorably condemned to a later, more acute suffering.

65. For a correct moral judgment on euthanasia, it is first of all necessary to define it clearly. Euthanasia in its true and proper sense must be understood as an action or omission that by its nature and intention causes death, in order to eliminate any pain. «Euthanasia is, therefore, situated at the level of the intentions or the methods used».76

66. Now, suicide is always morally unacceptable, as is homicide. Church tradition has always rejected it as a seriously bad decision. 83 Although certain psychological, cultural and social conditioning may lead one to perform a gesture that so radically contradicts one's innate inclination towards life, attenuating or nullifying subjective responsibility, suicide, from an objective point of view, is a seriously immoral act, because it involves the rejection of self-love and the renunciation of the duties of justice and charity towards one's neighbor, towards the different communities of which one is a part and towards society in general. 84 In its deepest reality, it constitutes a rejection of God's absolute sovereignty over life and death, proclaimed in the prayer of the ancient wise man of Israel: "You have power over life and death, you bring down to the gates of Hades and from there up" ([+[0]+]).

67. On the other hand, the path of love and true piety is very diverse, to which our common human condition forces us and which faith in Christ the Redeemer, dead and risen, illuminates with new meaning. The desire that springs from the heart of man when faced with the supreme encounter with suffering and death, especially when he feels the temptation to fall into despair and almost collapse into it, is above all an aspiration for company, solidarity and support in the trial. It is a request for help to continue waiting, when all human hopes fade. As the Second Vatican Council recalls, “in the face of death, the enigma of the human condition reaches its culmination” for man; and yet "he judges accurately by the instinct of his heart when he hates and rejects the total ruin and definitive disappearance of his person. The seed of eternity that it carries within itself, being irreducible to matter alone, rebels against death. "86

68. One of the characteristics of current attacks on human life – as has already been said – consists of the tendency to demand their legal legitimation, as if they were rights that the State, at least under certain conditions, must recognize for citizens and, consequently, the tendency to seek their realization with the safe and free assistance of doctors and health agents.

69. In any case, in the democratic culture of our time the opinion has been widely disseminated that the legal system of a society should be limited to perceiving and assuming the convictions of the majority and, therefore, be based only on what the majority itself recognizes and lives as moral. If, furthermore, it is even considered that a common and objective truth is in fact inaccessible, respect for the freedom of citizens - who in a democratic regime are considered the true sovereigns - would require that, at the legislative level, the autonomy of each individual conscience be recognized and that, therefore, when establishing the norms that in each case are necessary for social coexistence, these be exclusively adapted to the will of the majority, whatever it may be. In this way, every politician, in his activity, should clearly distinguish between the sphere of private conscience and that of public behavior.

70. The common root of all these trends is the ethical relativism that characterizes many aspects of contemporary culture. There is no shortage of those who consider this relativism as a condition of democracy, since only it would guarantee tolerance, reciprocal respect between people and adherence to the decisions of the majority, while moral norms, considered objective and binding, would lead to authoritarianism and intolerance.

71. For the future of society and the development of a healthy democracy, it is therefore urgent to rediscover the existence of essential and original human and moral values, which derive from the very truth of the human being and express and protect the dignity of the person. They are values, therefore, that no individual, no majority and no State can ever create, modify or destroy, but must only recognize, respect and promote.

72. In continuity with the entire tradition of the Church is also the doctrine on the necessary conformity of the civil law with the moral law, as stated, once again, in the aforementioned encyclical of John XXIII: «Authority is postulated by the moral order and derives from God. Therefore, if the laws or precepts of the rulers were in contradiction with that order and, consequently, in contradiction with the will of God, they would not have the force to bind in conscience...; Furthermore, in such a case, the authority would cease to be such and would degenerate into abuse."95 This is a clear teaching of Saint Thomas Aquinas, who among other things writes: "Human law is such insofar as it is in accordance with right reason and, therefore, derives from eternal law. On the other hand, when a law is in contrast to reason, it is called an iniquitous law; However, in this case it ceases to be a law and becomes rather an act of violence."96 And he adds: "Every law established by men is a law insofar as it derives from natural law. On the contrary, if it contradicts the natural law in anything, then it will not be a law but a corruption of the law."97

73. Thus, abortion and euthanasia are crimes that no human law can claim to legitimize. Laws of this type not only do not create any obligation of conscience, but, on the contrary, establish a serious and precise obligation to oppose them through conscientious objection. From the origins of the Church, apostolic preaching instilled in Christians the duty to obey legitimately constituted public authorities ([+[0]+]), but at the same time it firmly taught that "we must obey God before men" ([+[1]+]). Already in the Old Testament, precisely in relation to threats against life, we find a significant example of resistance to the unjust order of authority. The midwives of the Hebrews opposed Pharaoh, who had ordered the killing of every newborn male. They "did not do what the king of Egypt had commanded them, but left the children alive" ([+[2]+]). But it is necessary to point out the deep reason for their behavior: "The midwives feared God" ([+[3]+]). It is precisely from obedience to God – to whom we owe only that fear that is recognition of his absolute sovereignty – from which the strength and courage to resist the unjust laws of men are born. It is the strength and courage of those who are even willing to go to prison or die by the sword, in the certainty that "here the patience and faith of the saints are required" ([+[4]+]).

74. The introduction of unjust legislation frequently confronts morally upright men with difficult problems of conscience in matters of collaboration, due to the obligatory affirmation of their own right not to be forced to participate in morally bad actions. Sometimes the choices imposed are painful and may require the sacrifice of established professional positions or the renunciation of legitimate prospects for career advancement. In other cases, it may happen that the fulfillment of some actions that are in themselves indifferent, or even positive, provided for in the articles of globally unjust legislation, allows the safeguarding of threatened human lives. On the other hand, however, one can justly fear that the willingness to carry out such actions will not only lead to scandal and favor the weakening of the necessary opposition to attacks on life, but will imperceptibly lead to increasingly giving in to a permissive logic.

75. God's commandments teach us the path of life. Negative moral precepts, that is, those that declare the choice of a certain action morally unacceptable, have an absolute value for human freedom: they are always and in all circumstances obligatory, without exception. They indicate that the choice of certain behaviors is radically incompatible with the love of God and the dignity of the person, created in his image. Therefore, this choice cannot be justified by the goodness of any intention or consequence, it is in insurmountable contrast with the communion between people, it contradicts the fundamental decision to direct one's life to God. 99

76. The commandment "thou shalt not kill" therefore establishes the starting point of a path of true freedom, which leads us to actively promote life and develop certain attitudes and behaviors at its service. By acting in this way, we exercise our responsibility towards the people who have been entrusted to us and we manifest, with works and according to the truth, our recognition of God for the great gift of life ( [+[0]+] ).

77. In this new law the commandment "thou shalt not kill" is inspired and embodied. Therefore, for the Christian it ultimately implies the imperative to respect, love and promote the life of each brother, according to the demands and dimensions of the love of God in Jesus Christ. «He gave his life for us. We too must give our lives for our brothers » ( [+[0]+] ).

78. The Church has received the Gospel as an announcement and source of joy and salvation. He has received it as a gift from Jesus, sent from the Father "to announce the Good News to the poor" ([+[0]+]). He has received it through the Apostles, sent by Him to the whole world ([+[1]+]). The Church, born of this evangelizing action, feels the Apostle's exclamation resonate within itself every day: "Woe to me if I do not preach the Gospel!" » ( [+[2]+] ). In fact, "evangelizing," as Paul VI wrote, constitutes the joy and vocation of the Church, its deepest identity. She exists to evangelize.”101

79. We are the people of life because God, in his free love, has given us the Gospel of life and we have been transformed and saved by this same Gospel. We have been redeemed by the "author of life" ([+[0]+]) at the price of his precious blood ([+[1]+]) and through the baptismal bath we have been grafted into Him ([+[2]+]), like branches that receive sap and fruitfulness from the unique tree ([+[3]+]). Interiorly renewed by the grace of the Spirit, "who is Lord and gives life," we have become a people for life and are called to behave as such.

80. «What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we contemplated and our hands touched concerning the Word of life... we announce to you, so that you also may be in communion with us» ([+[0]+]). Jesus is the only Gospel: we have nothing else to say and witness.

81. Above all, it is about announcing the core of this Gospel. It is an announcement of a living and close God, who calls us to a deep communion with Him and opens us to the sure hope of eternal life; It is affirmation of the indivisible bond that flows between the person, his life and his corporeality; It is the presentation of human life as a life of relationship, a gift from God, a fruit and a sign of his love; It is a proclamation of the extraordinary relationship of Jesus with each man, which allows us to recognize the face of Christ in each human face; It is a manifestation of the "sincere gift of oneself" as a task and place of full realization of one's own freedom.

82. To truly be a people at the service of life, we must, with perseverance and courage, propose these contents from the first announcement of the Gospel and, subsequently, in catechesis and in the various forms of preaching, in personal dialogue and in each educational activity. Educators, teachers, catechists and theologians have the task of highlighting the anthropological reasons that underpin and sustain respect for each human life. In this way, by making the original novelty of the Gospel of life shine, we will be able to help everyone discover, also in the light of reason and experience, how the Christian message fully illuminates man and the meaning of his being and his existence; We will find precious points of meeting and dialogue even with non-believers, all committed together to bring about a new culture of life.

83. Sent into the world as "people for life", our proclamation must also be a true and genuine celebration of the Gospel of life. Furthermore, this celebration, with the evocative power of its gestures, symbols and rituals, must become a precious and significant place to transmit the beauty and greatness of this Gospel.

84. Celebrating the Gospel of life means celebrating the God of life, the God who gives life: «Let us now celebrate eternal Life, source of all life. From it and through it it extends to all beings that in some way participate in life, and in a way appropriate to each one of them. The divine Life is in itself vivifying and creating life. All life and all vital motion come from Life, which is above all life and above the beginning of it. From this Life comes to souls being immortal, and thanks to it every living being lives, plants and animals to the lowest degree of life. Furthermore, it gives men, despite being composite, a life similar, as far as possible, to that of angels. Through the abundance of his goodness, he draws and directs us who are separated. And what is even more wonderful: it promises that it will transport us entirely, that is, in soul and body, to perfect and immortal life. It is not enough to say that this Life is living, that it is the Principle of life, the Cause and the sole Foundation of life. Therefore, it is fitting for all life to contemplate and praise it: it is Life that vivifies all life. "109

85. In the celebration of the Gospel of life, it is necessary to know how to appreciate and value the gestures and symbols, of which the various cultural and popular traditions and customs are rich. They are moments and forms of encounter with which, in various countries and cultures, the joy of a life that is born, respect and defense of all human existence, care for those who suffer or are in need, closeness to the elderly or dying, participation in the pain of those in mourning, hope and the desire for immortality are manifested.

86. Regarding the spiritual worship pleasing to God ([+[0]+]), the celebration of the Gospel of life must be carried out above all in daily existence, lived in love for others and in the gift of oneself. Thus, our entire existence will become an authentic and responsible acceptance of the gift of life and sincere and recognized praise to God who has given us this gift. This is what already happens in so many gestures of dedication, often humble and hidden, carried out by men and women, children and adults, young and old, healthy and sick.

87. By virtue of participation in the royal mission of Christ, the support and promotion of human life must be carried out through the service of charity, which is manifested in personal testimony, in the various forms of volunteering, in social animation and in political commitment. This is a particularly pressing demand at the present time, when the "culture of death" is so strongly opposed to the "culture of life" and often seems to surpass it. However, it is above all a demand that arises from "faith that acts through charity" ([+[0]+]), as the Letter of James exhorts us: "What good is it, my brothers, for someone to say: "I have faith," if he does not have works? Can faith save him? If a brother or sister is naked and lacks daily sustenance, and some of you say to them, "Depart in peace, be warm and satisfied," but you do not give them what is necessary for the body, what is the use? So also faith, if it does not have works, is truly dead » ( [+[1]+] ).

88. All this requires a patient and courageous educational work that urges each and every one to take charge of the weight of others ( [+[0]+] ); demands a continuous promotion of vocations to service, particularly among young people; It involves the realization of concrete, stable projects and initiatives inspired by the Gospel.

89. These structures and centers of service to life, and all other initiatives of support and solidarity that circumstances may advise depending on the case, need to be animated by people who are generously available and deeply aware of how fundamental the Gospel of life is for the good of the individual and society.

90. People committed to volunteering are called to play a specific role: they offer a precious contribution to the service of life, when they know how to combine professional capacity with generous and gratuitous love. The Gospel of life moves them to elevate the feelings of simple philanthropy to the level of the charity of Christ; to reconquer every day, between fatigue and fatigue, the awareness of the dignity of each man; to go out to meet people's needs, initiating - if necessary - new paths where the needs are most urgent and attention and support are most scarce.

91. The demographic problem today constitutes an important chapter in life policy. Public authorities certainly have the responsibility to "intervene to guide the demographics of the population"; 114 but these initiatives must always presuppose and respect the primary and inalienable responsibility of spouses and families, and cannot resort to methods that do not respect the person and their fundamental rights, beginning with the right to life of every innocent human being. Therefore, it is morally unacceptable that, to regulate birth rates, the use of means such as contraception, sterilization and abortion is favored or imposed.

92. Within the "people of life and for life", the responsibility of the family is decisive: it is a responsibility that springs from its own nature - that of being a community of life and love, founded on marriage - and from its mission to "guard, reveal and communicate love".117 It is about the very love of God, whose collaborators and interpreters in the transmission of life and in its education according to the Father's design are the parents. 118 It is, then, the love that becomes gratuitous, welcomed, given: in the family each one is recognized, respected and honored for being a person and, if there is someone more in need, the attention towards him is more intense and lively.

93. Furthermore, the family celebrates the Gospel of life with daily, individual and family prayer: with it it praises and thanks the Lord for the gift of life and implores light and strength to face moments of difficulty and suffering, without ever losing hope. But the celebration that gives meaning to any other form of prayer and worship is the one that is expressed in the daily life of the family, if it is a life made of love and dedication.

94. Particular attention must be paid to the elderly. While in some cultures the oldest people remain within the family with an important active role, on the contrary, in other cultures the old person is considered a useless burden and is abandoned to his own fate. In such a situation the temptation to resort to euthanasia can arise more easily.

95. « Live as children of light... Examine what pleases the Lord, and do not participate in the fruitless works of darkness » ( [+[0]+] ). In the current social context, marked by a dramatic struggle between the "culture of life" and the "culture of death", a strong critical sense must mature, capable of discerning true values ​​and authentic demands.

96. The first fundamental step to achieve this cultural change consists of the formation of moral conscience about the immeasurable and inviolable value of all human life. It is of utmost importance to rediscover the inseparable link between life and freedom. They are inseparable goods: where one is violated, the other ends up being violated as well. There is no true freedom where life is not embraced and loved; and there is no full life except in freedom. Both realities also have an innate and peculiar relationship, which inextricably links them: the vocation to love. This love, as a sincere gift of self, 125 is the truest meaning of life and freedom of the person.

97. Educational work is closely linked to the formation of conscience, which helps man to become more and more a man, introduces him always more deeply into the truth, guides him towards a growing respect for life, and forms him in just relationships between people.

98. In summary, we can say that the cultural change desired here requires everyone to have the courage to assume a new lifestyle that manifests itself in laying as the basis for concrete decisions - at a personal, family, social and international level - the correct scale of values: the primacy of being over having, 130 of the person over things.

99. In the cultural change in favor of life, women have a unique and undoubtedly decisive field of thought and action: it is their responsibility to be promoters of a "new feminism" that, without falling into the temptation of following "machista" models, knows how to recognize and express the true feminine spirit in all manifestations of citizen coexistence, working to overcome all forms of discrimination, violence and exploitation.

100. In this great effort for a new culture of life we are supported and encouraged by the confidence of those who know that the Gospel of life, like the Kingdom of God, grows and produces abundant fruits ( [+[0]+] ). The disproportion that exists between the numerous and powerful means available to those who work in the service of the "culture of death" and those available to the promoters of a "culture of life and love" is certainly enormous. But we know that we can trust in the help of God, for whom nothing is impossible ( [+[1]+] ).

101. “We write this to you so that our joy may be complete” ( [+[0]+] ). The revelation of the Gospel of life is given to us as a good that must be communicated to everyone: so that all men may be in communion with us and with the Trinity ( [+[1]+] ). We cannot have full joy if we do not communicate this Gospel to others, if we only keep it for ourselves.

102. At the end of this Encyclical, the gaze spontaneously returns to the Lord Jesus, "the Child born for us" ([+[0]+]), to contemplate in Him "the Life" that "was manifested" ([+[1]+]). In the mystery of this birth, God's encounter with man takes place and the path of the Son of God on earth begins, a path that will culminate with the surrender of his life on the Cross: with his death he will conquer death and will be the beginning of new life for all of humanity.

103. The reciprocal relationship between the mystery of the Church and Mary is clearly manifested in the "great sign" described in the Apocalypse: "A great sign appeared in heaven: a Woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and a crown of twelve stars on her head" ([+[0]+]). In this sign the Church sees an image of its own mystery: immersed in history, it is aware that it transcends it, since it is on earth the "germ and beginning" of the Kingdom of God. 139 The Church sees this mystery fulfilled in a full and exemplary way in Mary. She is the glorious woman, in whom God's plan could be carried out with total perfection.

104. In the Book of Revelation the "great sign" of the "Woman" ([+[0]+]) is accompanied by "another sign in heaven": it is "a great red Dragon" ([+[1]+]), which symbolizes Satan, an evil personal power, and at the same time all the forces of evil that intervene in history and hinder the mission of the Church.

105. The angel's annunciation to Mary is found between these comforting words: "Do not be afraid, Mary" and "Nothing is impossible with God" ([+[0]+]). In truth, the entire existence of the Virgin Mother is marked by the certainty that God is at her side and accompanies her with his benevolent providence. This is also the existence of the Church, which finds "a place" ([+[1]+]) in the desert, a place of testing, but also of the manifestation of God's love towards his people ([+[2]+]). Mary is the living word of comfort for the Church in its fight against death. Showing us his Son, he assures us that the forces of death have already been defeated in Him: "Life and death fought in a singular battle, and, dead he who is Life, rises triumphant."141
